prize_parts.citation: For a visionary, densely patterned Romanian-language prose and poetry that turns memory, the body and dream into an inner cosmos of exceptional formal ambition and imaginative depth.

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B050, a single credited name, Mircea Cărtărescu. The exchange sharpened how I would defend it, but it did not change who I would name. On the common criteria the case is distinctiveness of voice, formal architecture and imaginative depth. In answer to the chair's question about which works I rely on, my case rests on Blinding (the first part of the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid, on public knowledge. In those books long, patterned sentences and large-scale composition join bodily experience, childhood memory, dream and metaphysical speculation. As the chair's questions invited, I have narrowed my claim. I now rest the whole-oeuvre argument mainly on the large prose, which I can judge through extended translation, and I put less weight than in round 1 on the poetic origin and the essays, whose coverage for me is thin. This is a narrower reliance on evidence, not a different preference. I also looked for a reason on merit or citation grounds to hold back from B050 or to prefer P000. I found none strong enough to record. The late-volume question is a genuine unresolved test, but it limits how much I can claim and does not show that the oeuvre fails the sustained-quality criterion. The citation names Romanian and joins prose and poetry, so that the credit stays within a single writer and one oeuvre. It does not claim more for the poetry than my evidence supports. My regional familiarity is not part of the argument, and I do not treat support from colleagues as merit. All of this rests on public knowledge, not fresh reading or independent verification.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains that the effect of this prose lies in syntax, rhythm and accumulation, and I can judge it only through translation. I cannot say how much survives. Colleagues have said the same, and the chair's question about Romanian readers or regional expert reports remains unanswered by anything in this record. A second reservation is that the very large late volumes may be self-enclosed. Mattson reads the recurrence as personal mythology, and Palm, Sward and Carlberg treat it as an open test. None of us has close-reading evidence to settle it. If the committee concluded that Solenoid and later work only enlarge the machinery of the earlier books, the sustained-quality claim would weaken and the citation would need to rest on the major cycles alone. A third reservation is that the case for a whole oeuvre is partly inferred from the major novels, since the poetry, essays and early prose are less well covered. These reservations do not currently outweigh the merit case, but I record them as live.

responses.point: Olsson says my repetition point applies to both his leading candidates. He argues that Cărtărescu's recurrence works across prose architectures and poetry, while Zurita's depends on a narrower generic range. He also says the committee should test whether the late novels deepen the project rather than circle it.
responses.response: I accept that the repetition test applies equally to B050 and B009. I would not let generic range do more work than it can bear, though. A writer can work in two genres and still circle one set of images, and I know Cărtărescu's poetry too thinly to say that the poems deepen the prose project. So I have reduced the weight I put on poetic origin and now rest the argument on the large prose. On Zurita, your framing that the citation must rest on the written sequences resolves my round-1 objection about the landscape work, which is why B009 is now my first alternative. The practical test I would propose for the committee is to compare individual poems within Purgatory and Anteparadise to see whether they develop. I cannot say it would favour B050 or B009, and I would not pre-judge it.

responses.point: Mattson calls the self-enclosure concern the strongest challenge to her own preference. She reads Cărtărescu's recurring motifs as the architecture of a personal mythology rather than mere repetition, and says this is a judgment from public knowledge.
responses.response: I take your distinction between mythology and repetition seriously, and I think it is the right frame, but it is hard to apply. A personal mythology is entitled to recurring images. What would show deepening is that each later volume poses a new formal problem, such as a new narrative method, a new relation between the body and the historical material, or a new register, and does not only replay the earlier solutions. I cannot demonstrate that from public knowledge, and I do not want my confidence to hide this. We agree that the late volumes are the weakest part of what we know. I would therefore ask the committee to name which volumes it relies on, and I would be content for the citation to rest on the major cycles if the late work cannot be shown to deepen them.

responses.point: Carlberg ranked Yan Lianke eighth because she cannot judge the Chinese prose directly and translated coverage is partial. She accepts that mythorealism is a real formal idea rather than testimony, and says she would reconsider if the strongest books are shown to carry the claim across the whole corpus.
responses.response: That is the right condition, and I cannot meet it with confidence. The Four Books and The Explosion Chronicles are, on public knowledge, the strongest evidence for the mythorealist poetics, and I find the grotesque and mythic forms inventive. I cannot claim that the later novels hold that level across a large output, and I raised that unevenness in round 1. This is why B024 is only my second alternative. I do not place it above B050, and I would not word any citation for Yan around his restricted status or reception in China. You and I share the judgment that merit has to be shown in the writing. We differ on how much weight the unresolved corpus question should carry, and I accept that your caution is a defensible reading of the same evidence.

responses.point: Palm says I am more persuasive on Yan Lianke's poetics than she was in her opening, which is a reason to keep him under discussion. She says it does not yet move him above a candidate whose formal project seems to her more consistent and more fully realized.
responses.response: I agree with that ordering. The consistency and realization of the formal project is the criterion on which B050 has to be tested, and I would not claim it is established. It is the same open question we both raise about the late volumes. Where I differ slightly is that I would not let the translated selection flatter one candidate more than another. My translated evidence for B050 is more extended, and that is an advantage for B050 only to the extent that a larger sample is more representative. I do not claim it is. I therefore treat B024 as a serious alternative that deserves a proper test of the later books. I do not treat it as a rival to the leading case.

uncertainties: Translation of dense Romanian prose and poetry: I cannot independently judge how much of the syntactic and rhythmic design survives, and no Romanian-language reader or regional expert report is in this record.

Corpus coverage: my knowledge of B050 is stronger for the major novels than for the poetry, essays and early work, so I now lean less on poetic origin and the whole-oeuvre claim remains partly inferred.
Whether the late volumes of B050 deepen the project by posing new formal problems or only enlarge it. If they only enlarge it, the citation would have to rest on the major cycles.

For B009, whether the written sequences alone carry the case in Spanish, apart from the landscape interventions and historical occasion, and whether individual poems within the sequences develop rather than repeat technique.
For B024, uneven quality across a large corpus that I cannot read in the original, and the difficulty of separating literary merit from the political context of publication and reception.
All assessments rest on public knowledge, not fresh reading or independent verification. This is a modeled committee recommendation, not the decision of the full Swedish Academy.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent from the supplied profile. I disclose the following as context, not as grounds for recusal. First, my own fiction and criticism concern Central European history and trauma, and I have ties to Prague and Vienna literary milieus. Cărtărescu is a writer from the wider Central and Eastern European literary field, so regional familiarity could be mistaken for preference. I do not treat it as evidence of merit, and I have narrowed my claim to the evidence I can actually weigh. Second, my 2025 public remarks concerned a different laureate and, like official prize remarks, may reflect a collective position, so they are not evidence of my preference here. Third, I ranked Yan Lianke second and Zurita fifth in my opening ranking. Zurita has since moved to my first alternative after the chair's argument about the written sequences. Both shifts rest on weighing the merit arguments and not on the number of colleagues holding a view.
